findings.title: Retry-count delete clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The deleteMany `where` is now `OR: [{method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now}, {retryCount > 1}]`. The second branch has no `method` filter. This cron only handles SMS, but the clause deletes any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) with retryCount > 1. Today only this handler increments retryCount, so the risk is latent. But the column is generic, and any future use by another reminder type would cause this SMS cron to delete those rows. It should be `{ method: SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

findings.title: Retry threshold does not match the described behavior
findings.body: The description says the reminder is deleted after scheduling failed twice. The delete runs at the start of the next cron run and removes reminders with `retryCount > 1`, i.e. >= 2. The sequence is: run 1 fails and sets retryCount to 1; run 2 fails and sets it to 2; run 3 deletes the row. That is consistent with two failures, but the delete only happens on a later run. Nothing reads or deletes after the second failure, so the failed reminder lingers until the next cron run. The `gt: 1` magic number is also unexplained.

findings.title: Error-path update is unguarded and can abort the whole batch
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If it throws (DB error, or the row was deleted concurrently, giving P2025), the exception escapes the loop. The remaining reminders are then not processed and the handler returns a 500. The original error is also never logged in that case, because `console.log` comes after the update.

findings.title: Reminders skipped before sending never increment retryCount
findings.body: Retry counting only happens when `message` and `sendTo` are both present and scheduling fails, or when an exception is thrown. If `sendTo` is missing (for example an invalid or absent smsReminderNumber, a common failure case) or the message is empty, nothing happens and retryCount is not incremented. Those reminders are re-evaluated on every cron run until the date passes, which is the problem the PR aims to fix. Likewise `!reminder.workflowStep || !reminder.booking` just `continue`s.

findings.title: Read-modify-write increment is not atomic
findings.body: The code writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, using a value read earlier in the run. If two cron invocations overlap, both write the same count and increments are lost. Use `{ increment: 1 }` for an atomic update.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry/delete behavior
findings.body: The PR adds retry counting and a new deletion rule that can remove reminders, but includes no tests for incrementing on failure, for deletion at the threshold, or for method scoping.
